title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on the Hours Base of a Waiting-Week Value for Claimants with a Recall Date
content:
**(1)** For a waiting-week value on Unemployment Benefit Claims, the hours base is the figure in hours against which fractions of the week's reported hours are measured when the week is valued.

**(2)** The hours base is 36 hours (the near-recall hours base) when the claim records a definite recall date falling on or after the handling date and no more than 240 calendar days after it.

**(3)** It is 34 hours (the far-recall hours base) when that recall date is more than 240 days after the handling date.

**(4)** Any other waiting-week value measures those fractions against the program's full-time hours threshold.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Definite recall date recorded on the claim | Hours base |
|---|---|
| 240 days after the handling date | 36 hours |
| 241 days after the handling date | 34 hours |
| None recorded, or a date already passed | The program's full-time hours threshold |
